meaning: The trained model in control of the arm, called once per decision on the arm's clock.
The input to a policy at one instant: on the SO-101, six joint angles and one image per camera.
The output of a policy at one instant: on the SO-101, six target joint angles.
One period of the arm's clock: 33.3 ms at LeRobot's default of 30 per second.
One attempt at the task: a table with one row of observation and action per tick, plus one video per camera.
The open-source robot-learning library the arm is recorded, trained and run with.
The part of a processor core that fetches and decodes instructions.
The part of a processor core that executes instructions.
The rate at which memory streams data to the processor.
The delay to fetch one item from memory.
The part of a GPU that does the matrix arithmetic of training and inference.
The part of a GPU that draws images by tracing light, used to render what a simulated camera sees.
The parts of a GPU that compress and decompress video.
A model that predicts what happens next if the robot takes a given action.
A design that predicts a compact internal representation of the scene in place of its pixels.
A policy built on a network that also reads a text instruction.
The set of event counters built into a processor.
The EC2 network device that lets many machines train as one, covered in its own dive.
